### Background
Burna Boy (born Damini Ebunoluwa Ogulu in 1991 in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, Nigeria) is a singer, songwriter, and record producer [SRC-face6e2e30b0].
He rose to stardom in 2012 following the release of "Like to Party," the lead single from his debut studio album, *L.I.F.E.* [SRC-face6e2e30b0].
His artistic lineage includes a direct connection to the origins of Afrobeat, as his grandfather once managed Nigerian icon Fela Kuti [SRC-8daf8e0406ac].

### Musical Style and Impact
Burna Boy's music blends African rhythms, reggae, dancehall, R&B, and hip-hop. [SRC-face6e2e30b0]
While he is widely recognized as a defining global voice of the contemporary African genre Afrobeats, he has frequently used the term "Afrofusion" to describe his distinct mix of sounds and cultures. [SRC-face6e2e30b0]
However, his claims of having personally created the genre "Afrofusion" have been noted as a subject of debate and critical analysis by music scholars [SRC-face6e2e30b0].

### Major Achievements and Awards
- **Grammy Success**: Burna Boy has earned extensive recognition from the Recording Academy, accumulating 13 Grammy nominations and 1 win [SRC-8daf8e0406ac].
His major projects, including *African Giant*, *Twice as Tall*, *Love, Damini*, and *I Told Them…*, have received widespread critical acclaim. [SRC-8daf8e0406ac]
- **Historic Wins**: He won a Grammy Award for his album *Twice as Tall*, marking a landmark moment for contemporary African music. [SRC-face6e2e30b0]
- **Global Touring**: He achieved milestone status by becoming the first African artist to headline and sell out major stadium and arena venues in the United States and Europe, such as Madison Square Garden. [SRC-8daf8e0406ac]

Burna Boy performs in Glastonbury, England, 2022.
Joseph Okpako/WireImage via Getty Images
Damini Ebunoluwa Ogulu was born in 1991 in Port Harcourt, the largest city in Rivers State in Nigeria. He would become known as Burna Boy, a singer, songwriter and record producer who rose to stardom in 2012 after releasing Like to Party, the lead single from L.I.F.E., his debut studio album.
With a growing army of global fans, he won a Grammy Award for his album Twice As Tall and has performed live at Madison Square Garden in the US. He recently revealed his sixth studio album , Love, Damini .
With music commonly described as a mix of reggae, dancehall, R&B and hip hop, Burna belongs to the broadly defined music genre Afrobeats (contemporary music mostly of Nigerian origin). But in an interview in 2015, he pronounced that his music was Afrofusion (a sub-genre of Afrobeats, but increasingly also a new name for Afrobeats, thanks to him). He referred , in one interview , to “when I started the Afrofusion thing”. Promoting Love, Damini in the US, he spoke again about creating his own genre from Afrobeats. He said :
I just mixed up a bunch of different sounds and different genres and different cultures and turned it into one genre called Afrofusion.
Burna Boy seems to be claiming to have created a new genre, Afrofusion, causing much debate . But even if he’s just saying that his music is a new genre of Afrobeats called Afrofusion, his claim is spurious at best. As a professor of marketing who researches West African music , I believe that Burna Boy’s claims are misleading, especially to the next generation of Afrobeats artists and their growing fan base.
Using the term Afrofusion may be clever marketing, but Afrofusion is a music style that has been in existence since before he was born.
In my view, the whole debate needs some historical context.
The history
Afrobeats (sometimes also called Afro-pop or Afrofusion) is an umbrella term used to describe popular music from West Africa and the diaspora that initially developed in Nigeria, Ghana and the UK in the 2000s and 2010s. It grew from Afrobeat without the “s”, a movement started by musician and activist (and Burna Boy’s idol) Fela Anikulapo Kuti .
It is no longer news that Afrobeats is taking over the world – written about in Rolling Stone and Time magazines. As the academic Samson Uchenna Eze writes : “Afrobeats is a broad, generic term for African contemporary popular music with rhythmic and harmonic influences of West Africa’s highlife and Afrobeat traditions and Euro-American funk and hip hop.”
Afrofusion, as the name implies, is simply fusing other genres with Afrobeat. The heavy presence of Afrobeat is coupled with anything from pop to reggae, dancehall to jazz, with endless possibilities. The style was happening long before Burna Boy debuted. As one music writer puts it:

About Burna Boy
Burna Boy has emerged as one of the defining global voices of Afrobeats, blending African rhythms, dancehall, reggae, hip-hop, and R&B into a sound that has helped expand the international reach of African music. Following the breakout success of songs like “Ye” and “On the Low,” albums including African Giant , Twice as Tall , and I Told Them… earned widespread critical acclaim and multiple Grammy nominations, with Twice as Tall marking a historic moment for contemporary African music on the global stage. Burna Boy became the first African artist to headline and sell out major stadium venues in the U.S. and Europe, underscoring his crossover appeal and the growing commercial power of Afrobeats worldwide. Known for his commanding vocals, politically charged lyricism, and richly layered live instrumentation, he often draws inspiration from Nigerian icon Fela Kuti while modernizing the genre for a new generation of listeners. A lesser-known detail appreciated by longtime fans is that Burna Boy’s grandfather once managed Fela Kuti, giving his artistic lineage a direct connection to Afrobeat’s origins.

By Elizabeth Clifford
March 12, 2026
All of Burna Boy’s Grammy-nominated albums and songs
Here’s a complete look at all of Burna Boy’s Grammy-nominated albums and songs, from his breakthrough African Giant to his latest global hits .
Between 2020 and 2026, Burna Boy , born Damini Ebunoluwa Ogulu, has achieved one of the most remarkable Grammy records for any African artist. With over 10 nominations and a landmark win, the African Giant hasn’t just collected awards, he has transformed how the world sees Afrobeats.
His Grammy journey is about more than personal success. It reflects the rise of African music from being labeled “world music” to becoming a respected, mainstream genre with its own dedicated categories at the Recording Academy.
In this article, we’ll explore all of Burna Boy’s Grammy-nominated albums and songs, highlighting their impact and showing how he helped establish Afrobeats as a true global phenomenon.
Burna Boy’s Grammy-nominated albums (2020–2026)
1. African Giant (2019)
Grammy Year: 2020 (62nd Awards) Category: Best World Music Album Result: Nominated
Burna Boy’s Grammy journey began with African Giant , released on July 26, 2019. The album’s nomination marked a major cultural moment, the first time Afrobeats had been seriously considered for the Grammys in the World Music category.
Although he lost to Beninese legend Angélique Kidjo ’s Celia , the recognition put Burna Boy at the center of a global conversation. African Giant masterfully combined Nigerian rhythms, Afro-fusion, and socially conscious lyrics, capturing international attention.
The album also performed strongly in the charts, reaching No. 16 on the UK Albums Chart and No. 104 on the US Billboard 200, setting records for African artists at the time. Hit singles like On The Low and Gbona went gold in the UK and Canada, proving that Afrobeats could compete commercially outside Africa.
2. Twice As Tall (2020)
Grammy Year: 2021 (63rd Awards) Category: Best Global Music Album Result: Winner
Burna Boy’s defining moment at the Grammys came with Twice As Tall , released on August 14, 2020. After missing out the previous year, this album marked his triumphant return. It was also the first year the Recording Academy renamed the World Music category to Global Music , a change that perfectly reflected Burna’s fusion of Afrobeat, reggae, and hip-hop.
With Sean Diddy Combs as executive producer and contributions from a strong international team, Twice As Tall firmly established Burna Boy as a global music powerhouse. The album soared to No. 1 on Billboard’s World Albums Chart, reached No. 11 in the UK, and climbed to No. 54 on the Billboard 200.
The Grammy win made Burna Boy the first Nigerian solo artist to take home the award in the Global Music category, a milestone that officially cemented Afrobeats on the world stage.
